title: Khadijah's caravan
hookLine: she sends him to Syria with her goods and her servant Maysarah, who returns full of praise

lines: OUT OF HER SIGHT FOR A LONG TIME.
cards: A merchant in Mecca has goods to send north, and she doesn't travel with them. Whoever carries them will be out of her sight for a long time, buying and selling with her money in markets far from Mecca.
She needs someone she can trust completely, someone who will bring back every coin, and she has heard a name. The merchant is a woman, Khadijah bint Khuwaylid. Today: Khadijah's caravan.

teach.b: Ibn Ishaq describes Khadijah as a merchant woman of honor and wealth, who hired men to trade with her goods for a share of the profit.
She has heard about the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: his truthfulness, his trustworthiness, his character. Yesterday's title has traveled. So she sends him an offer.
Take my goods to Syria, she says, and I'll give you more than I give the others. And she sends her servant Maysarah with him. He accepts.
The caravan goes north. He trades, sells what he brought, buys what she wanted, and comes back to Mecca. The sirah says the business did well.
But the profit isn't what the story lingers on.
It lingers on Maysarah, who has spent the whole journey beside him, seeing him far from home: in the heat, at the market, at the haggling table where small dishonesties are easy.
When they return, Maysarah goes to Khadijah and tells her what he saw.
Ibn Ishaq says his report included wonders: a monk's words about him, and angels Maysarah saw shading him from the sun. That's the turn. The goods came back.
So did a report, and it was about the man, not the profit. The Qur'an's word for something handed over like this is amanah, a trust.
In surah four, Pickthall translates: "Lo! Allah commandeth you that ye restore deposits to their owners." He restored hers, and more.
Later, in a hadith collected by al-Tirmidhi, the Prophet says the truthful, trustworthy merchant will be with the prophets, the truthful and the martyrs. A merchant, in that company.

how: Muslims remember Khadijah as a respected merchant and as the Prophet's ﷺ first wife, and honesty in trade is taught from his example and from hadith such as the one on the truthful, trustworthy merchant.

games.q: you're Khadijah. your goods will be out of your sight for a long time. you've heard of a young man called the trustworthy. what do you do?
o: hire him, offer him more, and send Maysarah along.
games.why: the sirah says she offered him more than others, and sent her servant Maysarah with him.

practice: Bring to mind one piece of work you'll do today, a task at your job, a chore, an errand, and picture a Maysarah beside you, quietly watching, not to catch you out, just to see.
Notice the one corner you'd usually cut, the shortcut nobody would notice, and choose, now, to do that part well. If you pray, you can ask Allah for honest hands; if not, just hold the choice.

wordCard.voice: Khadijah's caravan. The trading journey to Syria she entrusted to him, with her servant Maysarah, who came home, the sirah says, speaking of him with wonder. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: amanah, a trust, something placed in your keeping to be returned.

carryVoice: Your line: his honesty was the report. Tomorrow: she proposed. That's day seven hundred sixteen.
